post.caption: The Timur Ruby is not a ruby. It is actually a spinel, which is a different mineral from ruby, and names and dates of several royal owners are engraved on it. The earliest names the Mughal emperor Jahangir, in 1612. In 1851 the East India Company presented the stone to Queen Victoria, and Victoria's journal called the stones even more remarkable than the Koh-i-Noor. In 1853 Garrard set it in a gold and diamond necklace, and three smaller spinels share the necklace with it, along with diamonds. Some sources list it at about 352 carats, others at 361.
